subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Linear vs Switching Power Supplies
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Linear vs Switching Power Supplies.

hook.text: Linear regulators drop excess voltage as heat. Switching supplies chop and regulate — far less waste.

buildup.text: A linear regulator acts like a variable resistor. Simple, quiet, but efficiency can be as low as 30%.

discovery.text: A switching supply runs at 80-95% efficiency by rapidly toggling between on and off states.

twist.text: Switching supplies generate electromagnetic noise. Sensitive circuits like audio DACs still prefer linear regulators.

climax.text: Laptops, servers, and phone chargers all use switching supplies. Lab instruments often use linear.

punchline.text: Switch for efficiency, linear for silence — each excels where the other can't.

quiz.question: Why do some sensitive circuits still use linear regulators despite lower efficiency?
options: Linear regulators are cheaper to manufacture
They produce extremely low noise, critical for sensitive analog circuits
Linear regulators can handle higher input voltages
